articles.summary: On July 8, 2026, OpenAI replaced Advanced Voice Mode with GPT-Live, a full-duplex voice that listens and speaks at the same time. Here is what changed, how full-duplex differs from the old turn-based voice, and why it means voice is becoming the operating system for real work.
articles.title: GPT-Live Is Here: ChatGPT's Voice Now Listens and Talks at Once, Just Like 'Her' and JARVIS

articles.summary: Your computer can now do what you ask out loud. Not just write down your words, but send the email and add the meeting. Here is what to say, and what to try first.
articles.title: How to Talk to Your Computer to Get Work Done (2026)

articles.summary: In Spike Jonze's Her, everyone walks through the city talking quietly to an AI, each in their own bubble, and no one thinks it strange. As artificial intelligence grows capable enough to do the actual work, that calm, screen-free, voice-first world stops being science fiction. Here is why voice is the final interface, what the movie's world gets right, and how VoiceOS is building toward it.
articles.title: Voice Is the Final Interface: The World of 'Her' Is Becoming Real

articles.summary: On July 23, 2026, OpenAI brought ChatGPT Voice to its Mac and Windows desktop app. Powered by GPT-Live, it lets you talk to your computer to control it and steer multiple agents across ChatGPT Work and Codex. Here is exactly what shipped, what it can and cannot do yet, and how a system-wide voice layer compares.
articles.title: ChatGPT Voice on the Desktop: Control Your Computer and Direct AI Agents by Voice (Mac & Windows)

articles.summary: Apple is bringing the rebuilt Siri into CarPlay with iOS 27. Ask which trailhead your friend suggested and get the answer without taking your hands off the wheel. Here is exactly what ships, what you need to use it, what the safety research actually says about hands-free, and why the same argument applies at your desk.
articles.title: Siri AI in CarPlay: What Ships in iOS 27, and Why the Car Proves the Case for Voice

articles.summary: On July 23, 2026, Anthropic upgraded Claude voice mode. It now runs on Claude's more capable Opus and Sonnet models, can reach connected tools like your email and calendar mid-conversation, and speaks many more languages. Here is what changed, how to use it, and where a chatbot voice ends and a real voice layer begins.
articles.title: Claude Voice Mode Gets Smarter: Opus, Sonnet, Your Email and Calendar, and More Languages (2026)

articles.summary: We have all been stuck: a menu we cannot find, a setting buried three panels deep, an app we have never used before. A new kind of assistant changes that. It can see your screen, understand what you are looking at, and talk you through it out loud. Here is how screen-aware voice assistants work, and how to get one today with VoiceOS.
articles.title: AI That Can See Your Screen and Answer Questions (2026)

articles.summary: On a phone you draw a circle around something on screen and ask about it. Laptops never got that trick. Here is the same gesture on your Mac, and because you can talk while you do it, it goes further.
articles.title: Circle to Search, But for Your Whole Computer

articles.summary: Crop the screen, upload the picture, then type a paragraph explaining what you were looking at. There is a shorter way. Hold two keys, move your mouse over the thing you mean, and just ask.
articles.title: Stop Sending Screenshots to ChatGPT Just to Ask a Question
